script.title: The asteroid that ended the dinosaurs
sentences: Sixty six million years ago, a rock about ten kilometres wide hit what is now Mexico.
It struck at around twenty kilometres per second.
The impact released energy billions of times greater than the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima.
Rock was blasted into space and rained back down as burning debris.
Soot filled the sky and blocked sunlight, so plants struggled and food chains collapsed.
About three quarters of all species vanished, including the large dinosaurs.
But small mammals survived, and that opened the path that eventually led to us.
Is NASA's asteroid watch enough to stop the next one?

script.title: Why space is freezing if the Sun is so hot
sentences: The Sun's surface is about 5,500 degrees Celsius, yet space is brutally cold.
The secret is that heat needs something to travel through.
On Earth, air and water carry heat from atom to atom.
Space is almost a perfect vacuum, with nearly nothing to carry it.
So sunlight only heats what it hits directly.
That's why the sunny side of the space station can pass 120 degrees, while the shade drops far below freezing.
Astronauts survive with suits that reflect light and carefully move heat around.
Hot and freezing at the same time. Which side would you pick?
